questions.q: What does Databricks Data Classification do?
options: Uses an agentic AI system to scan Unity Catalog tables and automatically tag columns likely to contain sensitive data
Manually deletes any column containing PII
Encrypts every table in a catalog by default
Replaces the need for Unity Catalog grants entirely
questions.explain: Data Classification scans tables, detects sensitive data patterns (emails, SSNs, credit cards, etc.), and applies governed class.* tags to the matching columns.

questions.q: On the Data Classification results page, what does a classification tag's 'Unmasked user access (last 7d)' figure actually measure?
options: The percentage of users who accessed that classification's data without any mask applied, in the last 7 days
The number of tables scanned in the last 7 days
The percentage of columns that passed classification without errors
How many days remain before the next scheduled scan
questions.explain: It's the governance-relevant exposure metric: how much of the detected sensitive data is still being viewed in the clear by users.

questions.q: What does excluding a detection in the review panel actually do?
options: Removes the tag from that column, prevents it from being reapplied, and improves future classification accuracy
Permanently deletes the column from the table
Disables Data Classification for the entire catalog
Grants everyone unmasked access to that column
questions.explain: Excluding a detection removes the (incorrect) tag, stops future scans from reapplying it, and feeds back into the classifier to improve future accuracy.

questions.q: Per the lesson, why doesn't Data Classification by itself protect sensitive data?
options: It only detects and tags columns — an ABAC policy (or other access control) must still be built to actually mask or restrict access
It requires a paid add-on to enforce any policy
It only works on views, never on tables
It automatically deletes data instead of protecting it
questions.explain: Classification tags data so it CAN be governed, but access control (like the ABAC COLUMN MASK policy shown) is a separate, deliberate step that must still be taken.

questions.q: Where do Data Classification's detection results live as a queryable system table?
options: system.data_classification.results
system.access.audit
system.billing.usage
system.access.table_lineage
questions.explain: system.data_classification.results stores every column-level detection across the metastore, including sample values, and is restricted to account admins by default.
